entries.name: ComfyUI
entries.use_for: Build and run node-based image generation workflows locally, with an API for automation.
entries.why: The most capable open diffusion backend; huge custom-node ecosystem and a workflow API you can call from apps.
entries.summary: Modular node-based engine for building and running image generation and other AI content workflows locally, with an API for automation and a large custom-node ecosystem.
entries.best_for: Local diffusion pipelines needing fine control and scriptable workflow execution from apps.
entries.not_for: Needs capable GPU and setup; graph workflows are complex and not a simple turnkey generator API.

entries.name: Cropper.js
entries.use_for: Add an image cropping UI to a web app.
entries.why: Long-standing, dependency-free JS cropper with a v2 web-components rewrite.
entries.summary: Dependency-free JavaScript image cropper; v2 is rewritten as web components.
entries.best_for: Adding crop UI for avatars and uploads in web apps.
entries.not_for: Client-side cropping only; v1 and v2 APIs differ; no server-side processing.

entries.name: Diffusers
entries.use_for: Generate and edit images with diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, Flux) in Python.
entries.why: The standard library for diffusion pipelines with 1,000+ contributors and support for most open image models.
entries.summary: Modular Python library of pretrained diffusion models for generating images, audio and 3D structures, supporting both inference and training.
entries.best_for: Running or fine-tuning Stable Diffusion, Flux and similar models in Python.
entries.not_for: Needs GPU and model weights; designed for usability over raw performance and not a GUI.

entries.name: image (Rust)
entries.use_for: Encode, decode and manipulate images in Rust
entries.why: The standard Rust imaging crate, used across the Rust ecosystem.
entries.summary: Rust crate for encoding, decoding and manipulating images, with feature flags for formats such as AVIF, BMP and more.
entries.best_for: Rust apps needing image I/O and basic transforms.
entries.not_for: Basic manipulation only; Rust-only and not for advanced computer vision.

entries.name: ImageMagick
entries.use_for: Convert, edit and compose images in 200+ formats from the command line or bindings.
entries.why: The Swiss-army knife for image formats, available everywhere and scriptable.
entries.summary: Software suite to create, edit, compose and convert bitmap images in 200+ formats, via command line or language bindings.
entries.best_for: Scripted format conversion and batch editing across many image types.
entries.not_for: Slower and heavier than libvips/sharp for web pipelines; historic security issues from untrusted input, so sandbox policies are advised.

entries.name: imagor
entries.use_for: Fast libvips-based image processing server with Thumbor-compatible URLs
entries.why: Modern Go alternative to Thumbor/imgproxy; Apache-2.0 with URL signing and S3 support.
entries.summary: Fast, secure image processing server and Go library using libvips, with Thumbor-compatible URLs, URL signing and S3 support.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted on-the-fly image resizing behind a CDN as a Thumbor replacement.
entries.not_for: Server to operate; for in-process processing use a library like sharp.

entries.name: imgproxy
entries.use_for: Resize and convert images on the fly via URL with a standalone server.
entries.why: Fast, secure (signed URLs) libvips-based server; a self-hosted replacement for paid image CDNs.
entries.summary: Standalone server for resizing, processing and converting images on the fly, focused on speed, security and simplicity.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted replacement for paid image CDNs or in-app resizing code.
entries.not_for: Separate service to run; some advanced features are in the paid Pro edition.

entries.name: Intervention Image
entries.use_for: PHP image processing with GD, Imagick or libvips drivers
entries.why: The de facto PHP/Laravel image library for resizing, cropping, watermarking and encoding.
entries.summary: PHP image processing library with GD, Imagick or libvips drivers for resizing, cropping, watermarking and encoding.
entries.best_for: PHP and Laravel apps handling uploads and thumbnails.
entries.not_for: PHP only; not for advanced computer vision or high-volume streaming pipelines.

entries.name: Jimp
entries.use_for: Pure-JavaScript image processing for Node and the browser, no native deps
entries.why: Zero-native-dependency alternative to sharp for serverless and browser use.
entries.stable_reason: Mature pure-JS image library (v1 rewrite done); covers its scope without needing frequent releases
entries.summary: Image processing library written entirely in JavaScript with zero native dependencies, for Node and the browser, with a plugin system.
entries.best_for: Serverless or browser environments where native modules like sharp can't be installed.
entries.not_for: Slower than native libraries like sharp for large images.

entries.name: Kornia
entries.use_for: Differentiable computer-vision and image-augmentation ops for PyTorch
entries.why: GPU-native image processing that plugs into training pipelines, unlike OpenCV.
entries.summary: Differentiable computer vision library for PyTorch with image processing and geometric vision ops that run on GPU.
entries.best_for: Image augmentation and vision operations inside PyTorch training pipelines.
entries.not_for: Needs PyTorch; for plain image edits Pillow or OpenCV are simpler.

entries.name: libvips
entries.use_for: Process large images quickly with low memory from C or bindings (pyvips, sharp, ruby-vips).
entries.why: Streaming architecture that is many times faster than ImageMagick for typical pipelines.
entries.summary: Demand-driven, horizontally threaded image processing library that is fast and low in memory, used via bindings like pyvips, sharp and ruby-vips.
entries.best_for: High-volume or large-image pipelines needing speed and low memory.
entries.not_for: Less format and operation breadth than ImageMagick; C API unless using a binding.

entries.name: OpenCV
entries.use_for: Do computer vision and image processing (filters, detection, transforms) in C++ or Python.
entries.why: The most widely used CV library with thousands of algorithms and bindings for Python, Java and JS.
entries.summary: Main repository of OpenCV, the open source computer vision library. Its README is only a list of links (homepage, docs, forum, issue tracker) and contribution guidelines; extra modules live in the separate opencv_contrib repo.
entries.best_for: Computer vision and image processing work such as image manipulation, feature detection and video analysis, from C++ or its language bindings.
entries.not_for: Simple image resizing or format conversion where a lightweight library is enough. Some additional functionality lives in opencv_contrib rather than this repo.

entries.name: oxipng
entries.use_for: Losslessly optimize PNG files in build steps or CI.
entries.why: Fast multithreaded Rust PNG optimizer, a modern replacement for optipng.
entries.summary: Multithreaded lossless PNG/APNG optimizer written in Rust, usable as a CLI or Rust library.
entries.best_for: Shrinking PNGs in build steps or CI without quality loss.
entries.not_for: PNG only and lossless, so gains are modest compared with lossy quantization.

entries.name: pica
entries.use_for: High-quality image resizing in the browser (Lanczos, WebAssembly, workers)
entries.why: Best client-side resize quality; ideal for shrinking uploads before sending.
entries.summary: Browser image resizer using Lanczos filtering with Web Workers, WebAssembly and createImageBitmap, picking the best available technology.
entries.best_for: Client-side shrinking of uploads before sending to a server.
entries.not_for: Browser-focused resize only; not general editing.

entries.name: Pillow
entries.use_for: Open, edit, convert and save images in Python.
entries.why: The standard Python imaging library, supported by nearly every Python tool that touches images.
entries.summary: The Python Imaging Library fork providing image opening, editing, conversion and saving with wide format support.
entries.best_for: General Python image manipulation and format conversion.
entries.not_for: Not suited to heavy computer vision or very large image pipelines.

entries.name: rembg
entries.use_for: Remove image backgrounds from Python, the CLI or an HTTP server.
entries.why: Easy, local background removal with several U2Net/ISNet models; no API key needed.
entries.summary: Tool to remove image backgrounds using U2Net/ISNet models, usable as CLI, Python library, HTTP server or Docker container.
entries.best_for: Local background removal for product photos, batch processing or an API.
entries.not_for: Quality varies on hair and complex edges; model downloads and CPU speed.

entries.name: resvg-js
entries.use_for: Fast SVG to PNG rendering in Node.js, Deno or WebAssembly.
entries.why: Rust-powered, prebuilt binaries, custom fonts; pairs with Satori.
entries.summary: High-performance SVG renderer powered by Rust resvg, with a Node.js backend (prebuilt, no node-gyp) and a WebAssembly backend. Converts SVG to PNG with cropping, scaling and custom fonts.
entries.best_for: Turning SVG (for example Satori output) into PNG quickly in Node, Deno or the browser.
entries.not_for: Editing or authoring SVG, or raster image processing beyond rendering.

entries.name: Satori
entries.use_for: Render JSX/HTML and CSS to SVG for Open Graph images and social cards.
entries.why: Vercel's OG-image engine; works without a browser.
entries.summary: Converts JSX/HTML and CSS to SVG without a browser, handling layout, fonts and typography. Used for Open Graph images and social cards; pair it with a rasterizer such as resvg or sharp for PNG.
entries.best_for: Generating social cards, OG images and shareable graphics from components.
entries.not_for: Full CSS or interactive React (only a subset of CSS and stateless JSX is supported; fonts must be supplied).

entries.name: scikit-image
entries.use_for: Apply scientific image processing algorithms (segmentation, filters, features) to NumPy arrays.
entries.why: Well-documented, peer-reviewed algorithms that integrate with the SciPy stack.
entries.summary: Python library of image processing algorithms for NumPy arrays, including segmentation, filters and feature detection.
entries.best_for: Scientific and analytical image processing in the SciPy stack.
entries.not_for: Not optimized for production image serving or deep learning.

entries.name: Segment Anything 2
entries.use_for: Promptable segmentation of objects in images and video
entries.why: Meta foundation model and code for cut-outs, masking and annotation pipelines.
entries.summary: Meta's Segment Anything Model 2 for promptable segmentation of objects in images and video.
entries.best_for: Object cut-outs, masking and annotation tools.
entries.not_for: Needs GPU and large model weights; research code rather than a turnkey product.

entries.name: sharp
entries.use_for: Resize, convert and optimize images in Node.js (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF).
entries.why: The fastest and most used Node image library, powering Next.js image optimization.
entries.summary: High-speed Node.js module for converting large images to web-friendly JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF at various sizes, based on libvips.
entries.best_for: Resizing and optimizing images in Node servers and build pipelines.
entries.not_for: Needs native binaries (libvips), which can complicate some serverless or browser targets.

entries.name: supervision
entries.use_for: Reusable computer vision utilities: annotate, track, count and filter detections
entries.why: Model-agnostic toolkit that turns raw detector outputs into boxes, masks, zones and tracks with a few lines.
entries.summary: Model-agnostic Python toolkit for turning detector outputs into annotated boxes, masks, zones and tracks, with counting and filtering.
entries.best_for: Building video analytics with any detection model.
entries.not_for: Utility layer only; does not train detectors itself.

entries.name: Thumbor
entries.use_for: On-demand image resizing, cropping and filters server with smart cropping
entries.why: Veteran open image service with face/feature-aware cropping; drop-in behind a CDN.
entries.summary: Smart imaging service for on-demand cropping, resizing and filters, with face and feature aware cropping.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted image service behind a CDN with smart crops.
entries.not_for: Python server to operate; slower than libvips-based servers like imgproxy.
